identity.title: How Do Transformers Learn to Associate Tokens: Gradient Leading Terms Bring Mechanistic Interpretability

problem.claim: Explain how transformer language models learn semantic token associations from natural-language data.

contributions.claim: Uses leading-term gradient approximations to derive closed-form early-training transformer weights.
Characterizes transformer weight sets as compositions of bigram, token-interchangeability, and context-mapping basis functions tied to corpus statistics.
Connects the weight characterization to how transformer components capture semantic associations.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present closed-form early-training weight expressions and a three-basis-function decomposition for interpreting semantic association formation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that experiments on real-world LLMs closely match their theoretical weight characterizations.
The authors report that qualitative analyses use the theorem to illuminate interpretation of learned transformer associations.

narrative_sequence.summary: Semantic associations support generalization and coherent text beyond memorization.
The work studies association formation through training dynamics and leading-term gradient approximations.
Weights are expressed through bigram, token-interchangeability, and context mappings, explaining component-level association capture.
Real-world LLM experiments and qualitative analyses are reported as supporting the characterization and its interpretive use.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a mathematical weight characterization with a basis-function decomposition and qualitative interpretation.

lessons.interpretation: A mechanistic claim becomes more actionable when the formal object is mapped to interpretable components and then examined qualitatively.
lessons.application: For a theory paper, define the analyzed parameters in closed form, decompose them into semantically motivated components, and show how each component relates to the target behavior.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the target behavior cannot be meaningfully decomposed or when a closed-form approximation is not available.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the approximation’s range of validity, training scale, model architectures, datasets, or matching metrics.
It does not provide quantitative experiment results or details sufficient to assess the reported qualitative analyses.
